literal: Even than eating, that which was eaten digesting is sweet; in love, than union, lover's tiff is sweet.
translation: More delightful than eating is the digestion of what has been eaten; likewise, in love, more delightful than union is a lover's tiff.
modern: உண்பதை விட உண்ட உணவு செரிப்பது இன்பமானது; அதுபோல, காதலில் கூடுவதை விட ஊடல் கொள்வது இன்பமானது.
explanation: This couplet compares the pleasure of love to the pleasure of eating. While eating is pleasurable, the true comfort and health come from the proper digestion of that food. Similarly, while physical union is pleasurable in love, the temporary feigned anger or lover's tiff (ūṭal) is even more delightful because it intensifies the desire and sweetness of the eventual reunion. The poet uses the physical process of digestion as a perfect analogy for how a tiff processes and enhances the relationship.
